drivers: Recovery balance not provided, but ACWR cannot be calculated due to missing acute/chronic load metrics — a critical gap implying load monitoring is inactive
This month's runs (2) and km (6.0) are drastically lower than last month (10 runs, 51.3 km), suggesting forced reduction rather than planned taper
Aerobic TE dropped from 2.6 (Aug) to 2.3 (Sep), but cadence fell sharply from 149 to 148 spm and efficiency worsened from 14.12 to 15.42 ml/kg/km — consistent with fatigue-induced gait disruption

readiness.guidance: The athlete is not recovered enough for any intensity work or volume increase; the priority is restoring parasympathetic tone through low-stimulus movement and sleep hygiene.

monthly_review.summary: September shows a sharp, likely reactive drop in volume and pace consistency compared to August, with worsening running economy and signs of neuromuscular fatigue.
monthly_review.highlight: The 1.30 ml/kg/km deterioration in running efficiency — the worst value in the 5-month history — coincides with elevated HR at slow paces and reduced stride length (e.g., 65.7 cm on Aug 23 vs 78.9 cm on Aug 21), pointing to acute fatigue overriding pace gains.

goal_tracker.message: Matching last month’s 51.3 km would require ~45.3 km across 8 sessions — an average of 5.7 km/session — but given compromised readiness, chasing this volume is unsafe and counterproductive; recovery must precede volume rebuilding.

insights.title: Elevated HR at slow paces signals sympathetic dominance
insights.body: On Sep 1 (9:36/km), avg HR was 140 bpm — higher than Aug 21’s 133 bpm at 8:39/km and Aug 19’s 128 bpm at 9:12/km — despite slower pace, indicating reduced vagal tone.

insights.title: Worsening efficiency correlates with ground contact time spikes
insights.body: Efficiency declined from 13.42 (May) to 15.42 (Sep), while recent runs show ground contact >385 ms (Aug 23: 385 ms, Sep 1: 389 ms) — both outliers in the dataset — suggesting compromised neuromuscular stiffness and elastic energy return.

insights.title: Aerobic TE improvement masks decoupling risk
insights.body: Avg aerobic TE improved from 2.6 to 2.3, but this reflects fewer Z3–Z4 efforts (19% vs 34% in Jul–Aug) and more Z2 (74%) — not enhanced efficiency, but avoidance of threshold stress; true aerobic resilience remains untested.

insights.title: Cadence variability reveals instability
insights.body: Cadence dropped to 136–139 spm in three of last five runs (vs 157–159 spm in faster efforts), yet HR remained high — suggesting compensatory effort due to fatigue rather than pacing strategy.

recommendations.action: Zone 1 walk-run: 30 min total, 1 min jog (HR ≤120) / 2 min walk, repeated 10x on Tuesday
recommendations.reason: Maintains neuromuscular activation without cardiac or metabolic stress; aligns with compromised readiness and elevated resting HR trends.

recommendations.action: HRV-guided breathwork: 5 min morning box breathing (4-4-4-4) + 5 min evening guided coherence breathing, tracked via Garmin Body Battery
recommendations.reason: Directly targets autonomic rebalancing; no data on HRV baseline, but elevated HR at low intensities implies vagal withdrawal needing non-exercise intervention.

recommendations.action: Sleep extension protocol: Bedtime 30 min earlier than usual for 7 nights; no screens after 21:00; log sleep duration and subjective restfulness
recommendations.reason: Sleep debt is unmeasured but implied by efficiency collapse and HR elevation; prior months show no sleep metrics — this establishes baseline and leverages strongest recovery lever.

risk_flags.evidence: Efficiency worsened 1.30 ml/kg/km MoM, HR elevated at sub-Z2 paces (140 bpm at 9:36/km), ground contact >385 ms in two runs, and zero Z5 efforts for 5 months despite VO2max holding at 39–40 — suggesting suppressed output capacity
risk_flags.action: Cancel all Z3+ efforts for 14 days; reassess efficiency and HR response at 8:30/km before reintroducing threshold work.

risk_flags.evidence: Stride length dropped to 65.7 cm (Aug 23) and 74.5 cm (Sep 1) — both lowest in dataset — while vertical oscill held steady (~7.0–7.8 cm), indicating reduced propulsion force rather than form correction
risk_flags.action: Introduce daily barefoot calf raises (2x25) and single-leg balance holds (2x60 sec/side) to restore plantarflexor control before adding load.

weekly_focus.description: Prioritize nervous system regulation and neuromuscular coordination over cardiovascular stimulus; rebuild foundational movement patterns before reintroducing sustained effort.
